The code is the owner's {@link CustomerCode} identity {@code '-'}: the region 27 * derived from the owner's postcode (via {@link Locality}, so it disambiguates cities that share a 28 * name and falls back to the city table) joined to a hash of the owner's normalized telephone and 29 * last name (e.g. {@code 'NSW-3F2A9C1D'}). It is derived purely from owner fields — there are no 30 * sequence numbers — so it needs no persistence lookups. 31 */ 32 @Component 33 public class CustomerCodeGenerator { 34 35 /** 36 * Generate the customer code for the given owner from its region and identity fields. 37 * 38 * @param owner the owner being registered 39 * @return the {@code '-'} customer code 40 */ 41 public String generate(Owner owner) { 42 String region = Locality.of(owner.getCity(), owner.getPostcode()); 43 return CustomerCode.of(region, owner.getTelephone(), owner.getLastName()); 44 } 45 } 46

1 /* 2 * Copyright 2002-2013 the original author or authors. 3 * 4 * Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License"); 5 * you may not use this file except in compliance with the License. 6 * You may obtain a copy of the License at 7 * 8 * http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0 9 * 10 * Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing, software 11 * distributed under the License is distributed on an "AS IS" BASIS, 12 * WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied. 13 * See the License for the specific language governing permissions and 14 * limitations under the License. 15 */ 16 package org.springframework.samples.petclinic.model; 17 18 import org.springframework.samples.petclinic.util.Sha256; 19 20 /** 21 * The owner customer-code format {@code '-'}: the owner's canonical region, a 22 * hyphen, and {@code HASH8} — the first 8 upper-case hex characters of SHA-256 over the owner's 23 * normalized telephone concatenated with its last name. 24 * 25 *

The code is a stable identity derived purely from owner fields, with no sequence numbers, so 26 * every value the application builds from it (the membership number, its check digit and the 27 * owner's {@linkplain #regionOf(String) locality}) follows from the same region-and-hash identity. 28 * This class owns that format: it both builds a code and reads its region back. 29 */ 30 public final class CustomerCode { 31 32 /** Separator between the region and the hash. */ 33 private static final char SEPARATOR = '-'; 34 35 /** Number of leading hex characters of the digest kept as {@code HASH8}. */ 36 private static final int HASH_LENGTH = 8; 37 38 private CustomerCode() { 39 } 40 41 /** 42 * Build the {@code '-'} customer code for the given region and identity inputs. 43 * 44 * @param region the owner's canonical region 45 * @param normalizedTelephone the owner's normalized (E.164) telephone 46 * @param lastName the owner's last name 47 * @return the customer code 48 */ 49 public static String of(String region, String normalizedTelephone, String lastName) { 50 return region + SEPARATOR + Sha256.hexPrefix(normalizedTelephone + lastName, HASH_LENGTH); 51 } 52 53 /** 54 * Return the region component of a customer code — the part before the separator. 55 * 56 * @param customerCode the customer code (may be {@code null}) 57 * @return the region, or {@code null} when {@code customerCode} is {@code null} 58 */ 59 public static String regionOf(String customerCode) { 60 if (customerCode == null) { 61 return null; 62 } 63 int separator = customerCode.indexOf(SEPARATOR); 64 return separator < 0 ? customerCode : customerCode.substring(0, separator); 65 } 66 } 67

88 89 90 /** 91 * Save an Owner to the data store, either inserting or updating it. 92 * 93 * @param owner the Owner to save 94 * @see BaseEntity#isNew 95 */ 96 void save(Owner owner) throws DataAccessException; 97 98 /** 99 * Retrieve Owners from the data store, returning all owners 100 * 101 * @return a Collection of Owners (or an empty Collection if none 102 * found) 103 */ 104 Collection findAll() throws DataAccessException; ## Summary

I implemented customer-code de-duplication so that distinct owners always receive distinct `customerCode`s.

**The rule:** when the computed `<REGION>-<HASH8>` code already belongs to an existing owner, append `-<n>` with the smallest `n ≥ 2` that yields a free code.

**Where the logic went:**

- `CustomerCodeGenerator` (`service/`) — already the single unit responsible for "producing the customer code assigned to a new owner," so it now also ensures uniqueness. It builds the base code via the existing `CustomerCode.of(...)` (unchanged, still owns the format), then a small private `deduplicate(...)` helper walks `-2`, `-3`, … until it finds an unclaimed code. It gained an `OwnerRepository` dependency; `ClinicServiceImpl` still just calls `generate(owner)` and is untouched.

- `OwnerRepository` — added `boolean existsByCustomerCode(String)`, the collision check the generator needs, mirroring the existing `count*`/`exists`-style query methods.

- Implemented that method in all three repository implementations that back the interface:
  - `SpringDataOwnerRepository` (the active `spring-data-jpa` profile) — derived query, no `@Query` needed.
  - `JpaOwnerRepositoryImpl` (`jpa` profile) — JPQL `COUNT`.
  - `JdbcOwnerRepositoryImpl` (`jdbc` profile) — `COUNT(*)` on `customer_code`.

The `-<n>` suffix sits after the hash, so the region parser (`CustomerCode.regionOf`, which splits on the first `-`), the membership number, and the Luhn check digit all continue to work unchanged.
